findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow uses raw String for status and bool flags (is_validated, is_sent) instead of domain enums and typestates. Any combination of status/flags is constructable, including invalid states like status='sent' with is_sent=false or status='draft' with is_sent=true.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid lease state machine configurations can exist at compile time, causing silent logic errors, incorrect status reporting, or double-sent behavior.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with an enum `LeaseStatus { Draft, Validated, Sent }`. Replace `is_validated: bool` and `is_sent: bool` with a typestate enum `LeaseState` that encodes the workflow phase as a type parameter, making illegal states unrepresentable at compile time.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes a bare LeaseWorkflow and mutates it in place with no state validation. It does not check that the lease was previously validated before marking as sent. It returns the struct directly instead of Result, so no error path exists.
findings.failure_mode: A lease can be marked sent without ever being validated, or marked sent multiple times. No error is returned for invalid transitions, leading to data corruption or duplicate sends.
findings.fix: Change signature to `fn mark_sent(state: LeaseState) -> Result<LeaseState, LeaseTransitionError>`. Only accept validated states in the type system or return a typed error. Remove in-place mutation and return a new state.

findings.problem: id is a raw String with no domain validation. A lease ID could be empty, duplicated, or contain invalid characters. No newtype wraps the id to enforce domain invariants.
findings.failure_mode: Empty or malformed lease IDs can be created and used, leading to lookup failures, duplicate key collisions, or database integrity issues.
findings.fix: Introduce `newtype LeaseId(String)` with a fallible constructor `LeaseId::new(s: &str) -> Result<LeaseId, LeaseError>` that rejects empty/invalid IDs.

findings.problem: mark_sent performs string allocation (`"sent".to_string()`) and direct field mutation inside the workflow struct. This is imperative shell logic leaked into the core data model. The function has no pure validation logic separated from mutation.
findings.failure_mode: Core data structure couples business logic (state transition) with side effects (allocation), making it impossible to unit-test the transition rules in isolation and mixing pure domain logic with imperative mutation.
findings.fix: Separate pure validation (`fn can_transition_to_sent(state: &LeaseState) -> bool`) from imperative action (`fn execute_send(state: LeaseState) -> Result<LeaseState, LeaseError>`). The pure function takes no allocations and returns a bool or typed result.

findings.problem: mark_sent unconditionally sets `item.status = "sent".to_string()` and `item.is_sent = true` without any guard. The `.to_string()` allocation is also a hidden side effect in what should be a pure domain function.
findings.failure_mode: The string allocation can panic (OOM), and the state transition proceeds unconditionally even when the lease was never validated. The bool flag can become out-of-sync with the status string.
findings.fix: Replace with a pure enum assignment `item.status = LeaseStatus::Sent` guarded by a typestate or validated pre-condition. Remove string allocation entirely from the core.

findings.problem: No benchmarks exist for any performance claims. The crate has no bencher, criterion, or measured performance data.
findings.failure_mode: Performance characteristics are unknown. String allocations in hot paths could cause latency spikes or GC pressure if used at scale.
findings.fix: Add criterion or similar benchmark harness measuring mark_sent and state transition latency under realistic load.

findings.problem: No profiler evidence exists. Allocation patterns, CPU hotspots, and memory layout have not been measured.
findings.failure_mode: Hidden allocations (to_string on every transition) and boxed/heap data may cause unexpected performance degradation under load.
findings.fix: Run perf/callgrind/heaptrack to measure allocation profiles and identify hot paths before optimization decisions.

findings.problem: No allocation audit exists. The `.to_string()` call on line 10 performs an untracked heap allocation on every mark_sent call. No try_reserve or capacity planning is present anywhere.
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded allocation per call can cause memory pressure, fragmentation, or OOM in long-running services.
findings.fix: Eliminate string allocation in the core by using enum-based status. Add try_reserve for any collection growth paths and audit all heap allocations.

findings.problem: No second-ring command evidence (clippy, miri, or similar static analysis) is present. The code was not vetted for undefined behavior, clippy warnings, or soundness issues.
findings.failure_mode: Potential soundness issues, clippy-detected anti-patterns, or undefined behavior in unsafe code (if added later) would go undetected.
findings.fix: Run `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo miri test`, and include results in the evidence bundle.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or any performance claim
no profiler data for allocation or CPU profiles
no allocation audit for to_string() or Vec capacity planning
no behavior test suite for state transition invariants
residual_risk: Static review only with no commands run. The code has fundamental type-system violations that allow invalid lease states at compile time, and all performance/error-handling evidence is missing. The core domain model is unsafe by construction because raw primitives and bools cannot encode the lease lifecycle invariant.
